artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Reese and TE Bech complained that Philadelphia Presbytery erred in declaring their complaint out of order after Presbytery refused to allow any questions of TE Jason Hsu regarding his views on women deacons when approving his transfer to City Line Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that deeming parts of a complaint objectionable is insufficient grounds to rule the whole complaint out of order, though it agreed the proposed amends (removing TE Hsu) were not appropriate.

artifacts.title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Great Lakes Presbytery erred in approving Recommendation 5 of its Judicial Commission's report, which preemptively stated that Presbytery would not recommend or transfer TE Gonzales if he declined to demit or step away from ministry, because such action exceeded Presbytery's authority apart from censure after due judicial process.

artifacts.synopsis: Beverly R. Smith appealed her conviction on four charges (factiousness, gossip/slander, breaking membership vows, and contumacy) by the session of Covenant Presbyterian Church, which was upheld by Southwest Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, finding the documentary evidence insufficient to prove the charges and that the session committed multiple procedural errors including failure to produce witnesses, prejudice, and improper suspension from the sacraments before charges were disclosed.

artifacts.synopsis: St. Paul Session and others complained that Central Florida Presbytery erred in sustaining the report of a commission that investigated but did not bring to trial charges against TE John Hutchinson, and also regarding a related complaint against the Session of Christ Church, Jacksonville. The SJC denied the complaint, finding CFP acted within its right to determine investigation procedures under BCO 31-2, with a dissent arguing CFP failed to investigate the substance of the 45 specific charges.
